newsitem.title: UK: Dixons shares recover, fears over RRP fade.
newsitem.headline: Dixons shares recover, fears over RRP fade.

text.p: Shares in British electrical retailer Dixons Group Plc recovered strongly on Monday as fears subsided over the impact of an expected government abolition of a system of recommended retail prices (RRP).
Dixons shares gained 15-1/2p to 477 in early trade.
"To mark the shares down as agreessively as they were on Friday was an overeaction. I think there is a general consensus that the risks of a price war ensuing are overdone," said one analyst.

On Friday the Economist weekly reported that the Monopolies and Mergers Commission was about to demand an end to the use of the RRP and to require manufacturers to promise not to seek to control prices.
But the influential Lex column of the Financial Times newspaper on Saturday said those expecting a big drop in the price of electrical retailing goods will be disappointed.
Dixons itself said last Friday any steps to abolish recommended retail prices by the MMC would not affect its busines.

"As we have explained to the MMC, Dixon's does not use RRPs either in its stores or its advertising. Any potential abolition of RRPs is therefore not relevant to our business," said the company. On Friday Dixons shares fell to a low of 460p, before recovering slightly to close at 465p.
